In this experiment, you will investigate how the volume of water in a beaker affects the rate at
which the water cools.
Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 2.1.
thermometer
stand
beaker

parts.label: a
parts.text:
During this experiment, the thermometer must remain clamped securely to the stand.
Pour 150 cm3 of hot water into the beaker.
Place the thermometer in the water.
Wait until the reading on the thermometer stops rising.
In the first row of Table 2.1, record the temperature θ of the water at t = 0 and immediately
start the stop-clock.
Record the temperature θ of the water at times t = 30 s, t = 60 s, t = 90 s, t = 120 s, t = 150 s
and t = 180 s.
Remove the thermometer from the beaker and tip out the water.
[1]
